subject: Retention, egress & redaction playbook for PII exports
messages:
From: Olivia Hunt <olivia.hunt@brighthealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightHealth Security Team <security@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Security questionnaire follow-up: retention / export controls / subprocessors

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking the SSQ earlier this week. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy team as we prepare the DPA annex:

1) Retention windows: we need a clear mapping of how long raw PII (text spans identified as sensitive) is retained in any Redwood system for hosted and dedicated deployments. Please include what’s retained in ephemeral inference caches vs. persistent logs.

2) Exports and egress: when customers request data exports (for legal or operational reasons), what redaction/pseudonymization steps are applied by Redwood prior to producing the export? Are there scenarios where unredacted PII would be sent to subprocessors?

3) Subprocessor access: we need a list of subprocessors that handle export workloads or telemetry; for each, note whether they ever receive raw customer text and what access controls / KMS arrangements are in place.

4) Artifacts: can you share a dataflow diagram that shows PII zones, egress points, and where redaction occurs? The team asked for the current playbook used for export redaction.

We’re trying to close the DPA Annex this month. If you can send those items or a mutual action plan (MAP) with dates, that’d be great.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Hunt
Senior Privacy Manager, BrightHealth Solutions
[attachment: bright_ssq_v3.pdf]

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Hunt <olivia.hunt@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T12:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire follow-up: retention / export controls / subprocessors

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. Summary and next steps below; attaching our annotated dataflow and the current redaction playbook stub for your review.

Quick answers up front (detailed items below):
- Retention: raw inference inputs are ephemeral in the serving layer (TTL 5 minutes for active KV cache). Persistent telemetry/logs may contain tokenized hashes and metadata only; unredacted customer inputs are retained in persistent storage only when the customer has enabled exports or debugging and has explicitly opted in. Default hosted API: no persistent raw-text retention.
- Exports/redaction: we run an export redaction pipeline that applies deterministic pseudonymization followed by configurable redaction rules. Exports for legal obligations may be produced in a redacted form by default; unredacted exports require an approved legal request and audit trail.
- Subprocessors: model hosting partners and analytics providers receive aggregated telemetry only. Subprocessors that handle exported artifacts (e.g., file transfer and long-term archival) do receive export files but only after redaction/pseudonymization.

Requested artifacts attached: redwood_dataflow_20260831.svg (annotated), redaction_playbook_v2.pdf (redaction steps + decision tree). I’ve also attached a KMS custody matrix (xlsx) that maps which environment uses Redwood-managed keys vs. customer-managed keys.

Detailed notes:
1) Retention mapping (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Hosted API (default):
  * Inference runtime: KV cache kept < 5 min for active sessions; no raw-text egress to persistent stores.
  * Monitoring/telemetry: token counts, latency, error traces; sensitive spans are hashed and truncated.
  * Optional debugging export: raw text only persisted for up to 30 days and only with customer opt-in & audit log.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  * Similar runtime TTLs; customers may request longer debug retention under contract (explicit DPA clause).
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  * No Redwood-hosted persistent raw-text storage by default; retention is controlled by customer configs and KMS custody choices.

2) Export/redaction playbook (high level)
- Trigger: export request via console/Support/HSM-authenticated API (logged).
- Pre-check: automated policy engine evaluates the request against customer's DPA and the MAP.
- Redaction pipeline steps (see playbook PDF):
  1. Field-level classification using model + regex rules (PII fields marked).
  2. Deterministic pseudonymization for identifiers (customer-provided salt possible).
  3. Contextual redaction (free-text scrub) with conservative heuristics and manual review flags for high-risk exports.
  4. Encryption-at-rest with per-export envelope keys; transfer via SFTP / customer-specified storage endpoint.
- Audit: every export is fingerprinted and stored as a hashed record in audit logs (no raw content retained except in the encrypted export artifact).

3) Subprocessor access and KMS
- Model providers (in hosted mode): inference models access ephemeral payloads only, no persistent raw-text storage.
- Archival/transfer partners: receive only redacted/pseudonymized artifacts unless a documented legal exception exists (requires escalation).
- KMS custody: customers can choose Redwood-managed keys (default) or bring-your-own-key (BYOK). BYOK is enforced for Private deployments. See kms_custody_matrix.xlsx for mappings.

Proposed MAP:
- 2026-09-03: 30-minute review call to walk the annotated dataflow + playbook (Markus & Grace to join).
- 2026-09-06: We deliver a short addendum to the DPA Annex with explicit export wording and subprocessor list.
- 2026-09-10: Final confirmation and sign-off (target).

If you need, we can also produce a redacted sample export and a short annotated runbook showing the pipeline in action.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Security & Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T13:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire follow-up: retention / export controls / subprocessors

Chloe — added a couple of clarifications to your draft before we send to Olivia:

- Please make explicit that for Hosted API we never send raw customer text to third-party subprocessors. Model runtime partners may receive ephemeral payloads for inference but those endpoints are contractually forbidden from storing raw inputs.
- Note that telemetry providers (analytics) get only aggregated counters and sampled traces; they cannot reconstruct the original text.
- For Private deployments (VPC / on-prem), call out that customer-managed KMS is mandatory if they want absolute non-recoverability by Redwood; otherwise, Redwood can assist with a split-key approach (see matrix).
- Recommend including the redaction_playbook_v2.pdf (I updated step 3 to add an explicit manual review gate for exports marked HIGH-RISK).

Also suggest we prepare a one-page export flow for legal that lists the exact approvals and required fields (requester, justification, retention, expected recipients). I can draft it after the call.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Site Reliability & Ops | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Olivia Hunt <olivia.hunt@brighthealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightHealth Security Team <security@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire follow-up: retention / export controls / subprocessors

Chloe / Markus — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before the call: 

1) Reversibility: is your deterministic pseudonymization reversible by Redwood or subprocessors (i.e., keyed reversible tokens), or is it a one-way hash? We need the DPA language to reflect whether Redwood can re-identify.

2) Export sample: can you produce a short sample export (redacted and unredacted) for our legal/forensics team to validate the redaction heuristics? If you prefer, the redacted sample is sufficient; we just want to validate that PHI identifiers are removed consistently.

3) Timeline: the MAP dates look fine — can you confirm the 9/3 review call at 14:00 ET? I’ll send a calendar invite if so.

Also attaching a short excerpt from our internal policy to highlight the fields they will check.

Regards,
Olivia
[attachment: bright_policy_excerpt.pdf]
